newsitem.title: USA: CompuServe plans national marketing push.
newsitem.headline: CompuServe plans national marketing push.

text.p: CompuServe Corp said Tuesday it has launched a national marketing campaign, targetting high-end consumers.
The direct mail and print advertising campaign is the first since the company halted mass-marketing in the United States last fall.

"CSi attracts demanding consumers whose work and lifestyle needs are not met by mass consumer services, including a high proportion of business, professional and technical users," said Scott Kauffman, CompuServe's vice president of interactive services.
"In November 1996, we halted broad-based marketing to sharpen our focus on this attractive, growing segment. We left the mass consumer price wars to compete on value."

The campaign includes a 2.5 million direct mail drop, focused on business, professional and technical users; an effort to target consumers who ordered CompuServe software but failed to sign up; and a high-end advertising campaign.
The company said it plans a monthly Tip Sheet mailed to subscribers, e-mail marketing and an online newsletter for advanced members.
